preservation: All source identities and earlier art remain archived, including retired families and the withdrawn Oreviathan evolution. Active roster follows roster-curation.json; app LINE labels are stable family IDs. The duck-duck-grey-duck family is Tapduck, Dartduck and Greytag. Tugget/Lakernaut remains a two-stage line; Knotlet/Lasserp gains Knotitan. Birchit/Portabeau/Voyagear is the Water starter. Source IDs remain stable; display numbers are repacked in family order with pseudo-legendaries, legendaries and mythicals last. Kindlit/Rimepelt/Borealynx (MN_F125) is the Fire starter; Cindore/Pelletor/Mesablast remains active as the ordinary Iron Range furnace family. MN_271..MN_273 and MN_F124 remain reserved for the archived water proposal. Kensigard (MN_277/MN_F126), a user-chosen pure Ground Kensington runestone singleton, brings the active dex to220; rejected Vanesail and Sodger art remain unregistered and archived. Wildlife revision: keep Bobcast/Buoyostic, retire eight other weather families plus Torchcap, add seventeen species in seven woodland/wetland families, and retype Stackajack to pure Normal. Exactly220 active species remain.

families.theme: Lady's slipper and dance: a shy pouch blossom unfolds walking petals into slippers, then an elaborate orchid dress and hypnotic dance. Its unfolding petal dance develops gentle Fairy glamour as it matures.
Taconite and furnace heat: glowing ore gathers pellets into its body, then develops a blazing chest and cast-metal fists.
Skipping stones and hydrofoils: a stone-bellied water creature grows skimming blades, then broad wings that leap between lakes.

French-Canadian voyageur beavers: a paddle-tailed kit becomes an agile canoe-pack porter, then a sash-wearing expedition paddler with a straight wooden canoe paddle. The adolescent has no hat or paddle; the adult wears a tuque. Natural tails stay attached low on their bodies.
Wild rice and floating wetlands: a walking seed develops a root raft, then a hollow reed body sheltering smaller creatures.
Lake Superior agates: concentric stone bands reveal an eye, then unfold into nested shields and a walking fortress.
Monarch migration and royalty: striped caterpillar, gold-studded chrysalis, then cape-winged butterfly with crown-shaped antennae.
Rusty patched bumblebee and repair work: a rusty patch becomes metal armor repaired with hardened wax rivets.
Red pine, resin and campfires: a cone sprouts resin-filled branches, then branch-tip lanterns that preserve its living trunk.
Minneapolis flour milling: a grain imp grows millstone limbs, then becomes flour dust held together by rotating stones.
Morton gneiss and deep time: a folded stone hatchling unfolds into an ancient dragon whose limbs follow its pink-and-black bands.
Hockey: a puck creature develops skate feet, then a broad goalie body, catching hands and a self-grown ice mask.
Northern lights and the North Star: a magnetic spark develops curtain limbs around a fixed star-shaped core.
Loon calls and lake echoes: a resonating throat grows until its body can separate into overlapping echo silhouettes.
Living fishing lure: a painted jig with a hook tail becomes a fin-spinning lure, then a broad crappie-patterned adult with a large crown spinner blade.

Pancakes and lumberjack breakfasts: a self-flipping pancake becomes a dense springy stack with butter eyebrows and a syrup beard. Stackajack remains pure Normal; warm Fire attacks are coverage rather than its elemental identity.
Haunted logging axe: a walking hatchet becomes a double-bit axe with blade eyes and ghost arms growing from its grip.
Giant beaver fossil: petrified incisors and ribbed stone armor become a prehistoric log-dam body.
Leeches and suction pumps: a small sucker-footed trickster develops a bellows body that draws water and opponents toward its mouth.
Honeycrisp apples and fermentation: a crisp apple creature develops bubbling cider cheeks and a pressure-release bite.
Morels and hide-and-seek: a hollow mushroom cap becomes a maze in which its eyes appear at different openings.
Tamarack and autumn needle loss: a green sapling becomes a golden-robed bog spirit with fallen-needle attendants.
Thomsonite and fortune-telling: a concentric stone eye becomes independently rotating eye-nodules watching possible futures.
Pipestone and quartzite: a soft red claystone body bends beneath pale armor that locks rigidly in battle.
Mayfly hatches and fishing flies: thread tails and wing fans expand into a silhouette resembling a whole rising hatch.
Mosquitoes and vampires: a tiny pest develops cloak wings, a high collar and an expandable crimson abdomen.
Crayfish and bait traps: a crawler develops a folding cage carapace and interlocking trap claws.
Barn owls and silo acoustics: a round owl develops a hollow resonating chest and a facial disk opening like grain-bin doors.
Twin Cities skyways: a dangling cable creature becomes a suspended bridge body that joins its limbs into passages.
Duluth lift bridge: a folded truss becomes a counterweighted guardian that opens a passage through its torso by raising its arms.
Split Rock Lighthouse: a wick spirit develops a rotating prism crest and independently sweeping eye beams.
Tater-tot hotdish: a crisp tot becomes a baked casserole ogre with molten filling and golden tots along its back.
Cheese curds and state-fair batter: a squeaky springy curd develops battered boxing gloves and rebounds from blows.
Lefse and winter comfort: folded flatbread becomes a rolling blanket protecting its butter-and-sugar center.
Blueberry muffins: a berry imp burrows into dough and develops a split-top grin and blueberry freckles.
Birchbark canoes: living bark develops a canoe-shaped hull into which its leaf limbs fold defensively.
Snowplows: a shovel-faced machine becomes a heavy beast packing cleared snow into shoulder armor.

Butter-filled lutefisk cod: layered white fish flesh and icy translucent fins surround a golden butter heart. Its curled chin barbel, dorsal fins and forked tail form a clear fish silhouette. Butter ribbons follow its flank and fins; the butter is food detail, not fire or heat.

families.theme: Road slush, salt and winter grime: a grubby snowbank creature with ski feet, crystal teeth and dark slush under its skin.
Minnesota Nice and territorial geese: one welcoming wing and a polite smile conceal a second threatening expression.

Minnesota duck-duck-gray-duck and tag footwork: a golden tiptoe tapper develops a moss-teal chase-and-pivot body, then becomes the existing gray hand-crested sprinter. The forehead crest progresses one feather finger to two to the mature fan, while wing hands and broad webbed turn pads become progressively athletic. No clothing or carried props.
State-fair rides: a carnival spirit spins nested body segments independently while its face stays level. Its independently spinning segments are sustained by Electric power and playful Fairy glamour.
Lake Superior shipwrecks and warning bells: a rusted bow-shaped body contains a deep bell controlling anchor-chain arms.

Taconite and magnetic assembly: a banded ore dragon gathers pellets into armor, then becomes a heavy iron wyrm whose limbs are held together by magnetic rails. This is a cold, defensive counterpart to the hot furnace starter.
Prairie bison and rolling thunder: a dusty calf develops a resonating shoulder hump, then stores the thunder of its charge between broad horn tips.
Dakota skipper and grass-stitching: a grass-clipping larva sews a sod sleeping bag, then unfolds arrow-marked courier wings.
Prairie ground squirrels and seed-bank burglars: a small seed collector becomes a secretive vault-raider; cheek chambers and a burrow-shaped armored back conceal its stolen harvest.
Prairie chickens and drum circles: throat puffs become resonating drums; a semicircular tail acts as a sound reflector while its stamping feet keep rhythm.
Big bluestem and duelists: a three-pronged grass sprout develops jointed stem blades and a woven-root stance that bends without breaking.
Pasqueflower and predicting the thaw: a frost-insulated flower bud learns to sense spring before snow melts, unfolding a hood and then a cape of ice-veined petals.
Prairie loess and dust-devil dragons: a skipping dust knot develops an open spiral spine and a draconic head, then becomes a hollow earth wyrm held together by turbulent soil ribbons.
Milkweed latex and seed-floss parachutes: a sticky pod creature unfolds an irritant-fluff sail, then a broad canopy that scatters fictional poisonous down on prairie thermals.
Prairie snow fences and shelterbelts: a little living frost peg braces against wind, grows ice slats, then uses a broad snow-catching body and strong planted limbs to shelter smaller creatures.
Ore shipping and steam power: a compact harbor stoker grows into a broad lake-freighter creature; its hot boiler belly turns stored water into lifting power for ore-hold arms.

families.theme: Prairie wetland choruses and hypnotic toads: one resonating throat balloon becomes three differently sized poison-filled sacs; their chords make opponents drowsy. Chorip senses the chorus with Water/Psychic traits; mature Choirbog combines Poison sacs with a Fairy lullaby.
Prairie hares and pole vaulting: a bouncing youngster becomes an athletic vaulter, using flexible ears and spring-loaded legs to launch over fences.
Grasshoppers and wind-powered farm pumps: clicking leg joints become piston limbs; fan-shaped wings drive a little generator in its thorax.
Abandoned ore carts, mine fumes and ghost lights: a rattling cart collects fictional poisonous vapors, then becomes a spectral hauler carrying a glowing load of trapped fumes.
Prairie scarecrows and trickster shadows: a straw puppet casts an independent crow-shaped shadow that returns to perch inside its head; the shadow, rather than the straw, is the creature.
Sundogs and cold prairie skies: an ice-bright hound projects two warm luminous decoys on either side of its real face.

Prairie pothole wetlands and living filters: a low basin creature absorbs polluted runoff into a separate sludge chamber, carrying clear water in its back and expelling concentrated fictional poison when threatened.
Mining canaries and warning lamps: a canary-like creature has luminous air sacs and a chest gauge; it detects and stores fictional mine gases, flashing a warning before releasing them.
Wild teakettle logging-camp folklore and misleading opposite snowshoe tracks: a warm spout-mouthed creature grows a pressure chest and oversized feet pointing in opposite directions.

members.name: Doughlin
members.body_growth: A squat dough imp has two uneven curled cookie ears, a pale raw center and a single dark chip covering one eye. Its little palm pads leave warm round impressions.
members.silhouette: Round soft body, one tall curled ear and one chipped ear, short spreading palms.

members.name: Crumcone
members.body_growth: A tall white paper cone with one diagonal fold, a face on the white front panel, tiny paper-fold feet and an overflowing heap of chocolate-chip cookies. One curled cookie recalls Doughlin.
members.silhouette: Tall white paper cookie cone with a pointed base and curled-cookie crest.

members.name: Pailbaron
members.body_growth: A broad white pail body with a white rolled rim and high white arching handle. Its face sits directly on the pail beneath the overflowing cookies; crescent-cookie clamps and broad paper feet give a heavy final silhouette.
members.silhouette: Broad white cookie bucket, thick rim, high handle and powerful cookie clamps.

families.sprite_design: Only3-4 large chip marks, no tiny crumbs/particles or readable branding. Original pail-shaped anatomy differs from Casserogre food shell and Stackajack pancake stack. Ember glow is flat orange ink, no gradients.

members.name: Pipulse
members.body_growth: A small warm two-lobed creature rocks on paired toe pads; a pendulum-tipped tail and unequal ear horns keep a steady beat. A broad simple chest chevron visibly pulses between its eyes and belly.
members.silhouette: Two rounded chest lobes, tiny toe pads, one short ear and one long ear, pendulum tail.

members.name: Cadenset
members.body_growth: Two elastic chest bands loop into strong forearms, and the tail divides into counterbalanced beat paddles. It plants broad feet and uses alternating palm thrusts to keep companions moving in time.
members.silhouette: Broad elastic chest, two looped muscular forearms and paired tail counterweights.

members.name: Valorythm
members.body_growth: A second pair of smaller stabilizing arms unfolds from beneath the shoulder bands; the long ear becomes a sweeping conductor crest. A strong rescuer stance and four open palms make its protective role clear.
members.silhouette: Four-palmed compact guardian, high curved conductor crest and two sturdy rooted legs; no square appliance body, screen, needles or human heart diagram.

families.sprite_design: Rhythm is embodied in asymmetric crest, chest bands and counterweights, never detached music-note particles. Each evolution has its own warm cream/orange/deep-blue hardware palette. Large face/chest forms and four broad hands only.

families.theme: Red Wing clay craft and salt-glazed stoneware: a kneading clay creature fires its own surface into patterned protective pottery planes.

Museum holds stoneware, pottery, manufacturing photographs and worker-made folk-art pieces.
Tan salt glaze and cobalt decoration support restrained clay/blue palette inspiration.

members.name: Kilnook
members.body_growth: A warm clay kneader has a broad hollow cheek, two thick loop arms and a curled clay ribbon tail; its belly stays soft and its footprints have a thumb-pressed spiral.
members.silhouette: Low squashy mound with large loop elbows and one upright ribbon tail.

members.name: Glazaur
members.body_growth: Firing gives it broad rigid glaze plates, a wide ceramic lip-mask with a short blunt muzzle and a heavy crock-like belly carried on four short legs. Handle-like shoulder loops lock down as armor, and cobalt-like marks follow the plate joints.
members.silhouette: Squat ceramic beast with a broad lip-mask and short blunt muzzle with paired shoulder loops, round belly and upturned thick tail; no furnace door or chimney.

families.sprite_design: No logos, numbers or copied pottery trademarks. Ceramic motifs are broad blue swirls, not fine glaze texture. Warm clay becomes lighter fired planes; keep visibly distinct from the metal furnace starter. Use a broad lip-mask, never the long spout/arched body of Contrakett.

families.theme: Wabasha sandstone caves, secret knocks and swing music: a muffled cave echo develops its own syncopated body and bends arches into dancing limbs.
families.habitat: Echoing sandstone rooms and old performance cellars on the St Paul riverfront. A fictional living musical echo, not the spirit of an actual person or historic death.

map_placement.status: proposed habitat only; no map or encounter mutation

members.name: Hushuff
members.body_growth: A shy hollow sandstone head nestles between two large palm-like ear shells; its short arms press together to silence its own echo. Two offset eye slits resemble a half-open secret doorway.
members.silhouette: Round hooded head, oversized ear-palms and a short kinked echo tail.

members.name: Scatacomb
members.body_growth: Ribbed torso arches stretch apart like a folded dance hall, two long spring arms end in clapping stone palms, and broad curved feet stamp syncopated steps. A cape-like rear arch and bent head make its shadow seem to dance a beat later.
members.silhouette: Tall arched rib body, two huge raised palms and wide bent stamping feet; no human suit, gun, hat or separate instrument.

families.sprite_design: Only3 torso arches, large hands and simple eyes. Music comes through pose and offbeat structural rhythm; no musical-note particles, tiny architecture or real-person likeness.

families.theme: Mississippi freshwater mussels and fishlike mantle lures: a shell-dwelling trickster grows its soft lure into an attached stage puppet, keeping its real face sheltered within.
families.habitat: Quiet submerged river ledges and protected mussel beds along the Twin Cities Mississippi corridor; this is the natural soft-mantle counterpart to the metal Jiglet/Trollure fishing lure.

map_placement.status: proposed habitat only; no map or encounter mutation

sources.supports: Documents native mussels and their habitat in the Twin Cities Mississippi corridor.
Explains fishlike mantle-lure adaptations; psychic puppetry is fictional.

members.name: Mimuss
members.body_growth: A squat ribbed shell walks on one broad folded foot. A thick short mantle stalk above its hinge carries a tiny false fish face, while the real eyes peer through a narrow shell opening.
members.silhouette: Compact shell with one large foot and one hooked fish-face lure stalk.

members.name: Mantasm
members.body_growth: The shell opens into a wide theater-like hood; four thick mantle arms unfold around its true face, two supporting larger false fish heads with exaggerated eye spots. It manipulates opponents attention by moving the false faces in opposite directions.
members.silhouette: Broad split shell canopy with two attached fish-puppet stalks and a dark central real face; no detached creatures, thin strings or metal hooks.

families.sprite_design: Two fishlike puppet heads at most, thick attached soft stalks and large shell ribs. Make true eyes clear inside the shell. Per-species pearl/blue/ink palettes, no metallic spinner silhouette.

families.theme: Mississippi paddlefish electroreception and signal triangulation: a sensory spoon snout branches into an organic phased-array crest that reads hidden movement.
families.habitat: Wide calm channels and plankton-rich bends near the riverfront cities; source paddlefish distribution includes the Mississippi below St Anthony Falls.

map_placement.status: proposed habitat only; no map or encounter mutation

sources.supports: Places paddlefish in the Mississippi and St Croix, including Lake Pepin.
Describes snout sensors detecting electrical signals from plankton and filtering gill rakers; generating electricity and psychic triangulation are fiction.

members.name: Pinglet
members.body_growth: A chunky little river creature has a very broad rounded spoon snout, tiny side fins and a thick forked tail. A single notch down the paddle holds two luminous sensor pits, and the mouth is tucked beneath.
members.silhouette: Low pill-shaped body behind an oversized rounded sensory paddle.

members.name: Paddarray
members.body_growth: Its paddle branches into three broad blunt prongs arranged as a Y-shaped sensory fan; a thick pleated gill collar spreads behind the head and the tail grows three wide sculling lobes. It turns the prongs independently before darting along a chosen signal.
members.silhouette: Huge three-pronged head fan, broad collar and short strong tail; not an ordinary paddlefish with a lightning mark or a fish attached to a radar dish.

families.sprite_design: Keep three large solid prongs and collar folds, no tiny dots, waves or detached radar rings. Electrical cyan/amber and deep-violet inks distinguish species while staying related.

families.theme: Princess Kay of the Milky Way and Minnesota fair butter carving: a chilled butter chip sculpts itself into an original dairy princess, with a carved tiara, curled butter-shaving collar and star-cut sash. Its royal skirt and hands are solid butter. The chill preserves a Fairy enchantment within the animated carving.
families.habitat: Cold-storage corners of city dairy markets and traveling fair displays near St Paul. Separate from Lutebrisk: a solid self-sculpting butter creature, not jelly with a butter heart.

map_placement.status: proposed habitat only; no map or encounter mutation

sources.supports: Princess Kay and her court have likenesses carved from90-pound butter blocks at the fair; the creature is an original carved-butter princess, not a portrait.
Princess Kay of the Milky Way is a Minnesota dairy ambassador; the refrigerated rotating butter-sculpture tradition inspires the fictional tiara and star sash.

members.name: Chislet
members.body_growth: A small uneven butter block has two short wedge feet and a large chisel-shaped forearm; a curled shaving above one eye becomes a questioning eyebrow. It chips away a corner to free its other hand.
members.silhouette: Asymmetric cuboid with one wedge arm, curled eyebrow and stub feet.

members.name: Buttermuse
members.body_growth: A poised thick butter princess has a three-point carved tiara integrated with its spiral curl, a curled shaving collar, two gracious solid butter hands and a flared scalloped butter skirt. A white diagonal sash bears one blue star cut; two wedge feet brace the base.
members.silhouette: Three-point butter tiara, spiral curl, broad scalloped royal base and two open butter hands; original monster face, no real-person portrait.

families.sprite_design: Accepted Chislet preserved. Buttermuse keeps the butter-and-cold-blue palette and curl identity while becoming a princess. Tiara, sash, carved skirt and eyes must read at54 native pixels; no giant fighting fists or fine jewelry.

families.habitat: Clean rocky creeks and riparian shade on the Driftless Trail; case-building is a general caddisfly inspiration, not a claim that a particular rare species lives on the authored route.

map_placement.status: proposed habitat only; no map or encounter mutation

sources.supports: Explains caddisfly larvae using silk to join stone/plant pieces into protective cases. Mosaic-powered wings and illusions are fiction.

members.name: Tesslarv
members.body_growth: A determined larva pulls a squat three-sided stone case with six little gripping feet. Three broad contrasting pebble slabs fit like tiles around its raised face, and two feelers act like short measuring arms.
members.silhouette: Angular triangular case with a broad exposed face and short gripping front feet.

members.name: Mothosaic
members.body_growth: The case tiles become four large wing panels joined by thick silk veins, folding into a tent over a compact insect body. The broad face and measuring feelers remain; it tilts the panels to make its outline seem farther away or broken into separate shapes.
members.silhouette: Four tiled wing planes in a stepped canopy, stout center and two short measuring antennae; no ordinary butterfly pattern or detached tile swarm.

families.sprite_design: Only3-4 large mosaic tiles per wing pair; no tiny tessellation or glass gradients. Larva stone case and adult panel hinges show actual transformation. Separate from Mayquip hatch/fishing-fly theme and Dakotaskip grass stitching.

members.name: Torchcap
members.body_growth: A squat charcoal creature has a tall curled vent-cap grown from its head, two spring-bellows forearms and huge wick-knuckle fists. A broad warm chest and jaunty braced feet suggest a performer warming up; an angular grin sits under the cap, with one sweeping solid ember eyebrow.
members.silhouette: Tall curved vent-cap above broad low chest, two giant rounded torch fists and short planted legs; no human costume, vehicle, carried torch or detached flame particles.

families.sprite_design: One strong cap curl, two broad fists and a clear face. Black coal is colored dark-red/brown planes rather than an all-black body; bright orange heat seams stay flat. Distinct from Wickit candle spirit and furnace golems.

families.theme: Red River sugarbeets and stored energy: living taproots become energy-storing bulbs, then open root-rings with leaf terminals and four soil contacts. Electricity is original fantasy, not real beet biology.

Broad energy-storing bulb with thick conducting root forearms, split feet and broad leaf-terminal shoulders.
Broad organic OPEN RING taproot torso, one clean central opening, FOUR rooted feet, huge leaf-terminal shoulders and small clear-eyed upper root head. No cables, appliances or bolt decals.

families.theme: Smoldering peat and buried memory: a warm peat crumb grows a protective dark crust, then separates into layered peat slabs around an old ember spirit. It is a quiet underground ember, distinct from pine-resin campfire creatures and furnace-ore starters.
evolution_design: A low peat crumb has one hot eye slit, forked root feet and a single blunt breathing vent.

The crumb becomes a broad four-rooted crust creature with two thick peat-clod forearms and three dorsal air slots; it can pull the ember face under its crust. The three air slots store and exhale fictional irritant ember-fumes as a defensive vent system.
The layered crust rises into four broad floating peat plates framing a hot face; the lower layers taper into one heavy smoky root spiral and the forearms become spectral clods.

silhouettes.front: Low rectangular ember crumb, fork feet, one blunt vent.
silhouettes.back: Large back of peat crust and vent; feet below crop.

silhouettes.front: Wide low four-root crust, thick clod forearms.
silhouettes.back: Peat shoulders and three air-slot bases fill width.

silhouettes.front: Tall separated peat slabs, broad ghost arms, one spiral lower body.
silhouettes.back: Upper slab backs and ember-core crown, lower spiral out of frame.

Three knuckled ice lobes grow around a dark charge core; broad short arms and a split crown replace the seed outline.
A low anvil-shaped storm body spans four chunky hail feet; two thick side fins and a split conducting crown grow directly from the layered ice, with one jagged physical tail.

silhouettes.back: Back of bead and broad crown edge.

sources.fantasy_extension: Layered hail bodies store fictional electrical charge; no claim of a new documented species.

families.theme: Eskers as preserved underground rivers: a hooked gravel ridge learns to move, then becomes an articulated six-foot landform dragon whose raised spine follows a vanished meltwater channel.
evolution_design: A short hooked gravel wedge has two underside feet and an eye beneath its raised ridge.
Three thick arching ridge segments join a broad snout and short foreclaws, leaving two clean gaps below the spine.

Six strong pillar feet support five broad interlocked ridge segments, a blunt river-channel dragon head and a gravel fan tail. It is a heavy landform crawler, not a thin snake or a recolored Loessurge.

silhouettes.front: Hooked gravel wedge with low eye.
silhouettes.back: Raised ridge nape, lower feet cropped.

silhouettes.front: Three articulated arches and short foreclaws.
silhouettes.back: Broad ridge shoulders with two seams.

silhouettes.front: Long low five-segment ridge crawler on six pillar feet.
silhouettes.back: Close blunt head, first two ridge shoulders and gravel crown; long body exits bottom.

families.theme: Popcorn pressure and springing punches: a hard warm kernel splits into an airy fighter whose tough seed hulls become rebounding knuckles. This family is the popping seed itself, with no griddle, pot, appliance or hotdish-ogy body.
evolution_design: A hard pointed kernel stands on two split hull feet; two eye whites sit above a small pressure seam.
The shell opens around a broad starch puff; one large puff forearm and one hard hull forearm create a lopsided springing pose.
Three broad popped-starch lobes form a light muscular torso, paired curved hull fists spring from short puff arms, and two strong bent hull feet brace its rebounds.

silhouettes.back: Back hull seam and kernel crown.

families.theme: Plains hognose bluffing and stage illusions: a shovel-snouted bluffer grows a false second face in its flared neck, rolling its body to swap which face an opponent sees. The theme is embodied in anatomy, not a snake wearing a theater mask.
evolution_design: A squat S-folded body, upturned shovel nose and two huge false-eye cheek patches exaggerate its bluff; the neck folds into a broad heart shape.

The neck opens into a large double-faced false jaw, while the real small head hides beneath the upturned snout; a broad curved tail can roll the body onto its back, and the shadow of the false face moves independently.

silhouettes.front: Compact heart-neck bluffer with blunt shovel nose, no thin stretched snake body.
silhouettes.back: Back of folded neck and broad false-eye patches, tail exits crop.

silhouettes.back: Back of double-faced neck mantle; real face turned away and lower coil cropped.

sources.evidence: Plains hog-nosed snakes use upturned noses, display false eye patches, flatten their heads and bluff or play dead.
sources.fantasy_extension: A fictional false-face anatomy and independent shadow dramatize the bluffing behavior.

families.theme: Prairie smoke and disappearing acts: nodding flower buds conceal an imp; the feathery seed plumes then become the imp body itself, scattering false silhouettes in the wind. Its smoke is seed fluff, not another fire monster.
evolution_design: Three nodding buds fold over one hidden face on a low leaf rosette; two thick root fingers let it peek out and close its cloak.

The root body disappears as three broad seed-plume fans coil into a floating cloak with one dark eye slit and two large plume hands. Its growing-season leaf mass becomes a ghostly seed-body, explaining the type change. The broad seed-plume fans actively lift and steer its light body on prairie thermals.

silhouettes.front: Low rosette with three hanging bud hoods and two root fingers.
silhouettes.back: Back of nodding bud cluster and rosette shoulders.

silhouettes.front: Floating three-fan plume cloak with two broad hands; no tiny hair detail.
silhouettes.back: Large plume nape and cloak shoulders, lower wind tail cropped.

families.habitat: Dry prairie remnants and open glacial ridges; seed-plume stage most common after spring flowering.

sources.evidence: Prairie smoke has nodding spring flowers and feathery seed plumes resembling smoke.
sources.fantasy_extension: Flowers become an illusion cloak, then living ghost seed plumes; the supernatural aspect is original.

families.theme: Light pillars and mirror alignment: an ice-crystal prism creature learns to stack reflections, growing two offset mirror columns and redirecting a light source into a false vertical image. evolution_design: A floating hexagonal prism with one dark face panel and two thick horizontal mirror tabs.
Two unequal upright prism shoulders flank a small central head and a broad wedge torso; the mirror tabs become articulated panel arms that can face the same direction or oppose one another.

silhouettes.front: One hexagonal prism, two broad mirror tabs.
silhouettes.back: Faceted nape and panel tabs fill close frame.

silhouettes.front: Offset twin prism shoulders, wedge torso and two panel arms.
silhouettes.back: Back faces of upper prisms and shoulders; lower body cropped.

families.habitat: Cold clear nights near prairie towns and open-field lamps, proposed conditional ordinary encounters.

sources.evidence: Minnesota light pillars arise when aligned ice crystals reflect light; the DNR documents observations around St. Cloud and the Twin Cities.
sources.fantasy_extension: A fictional crystal creature controls reflection alignment and stores the redirected light as electrical power.

families.theme: Fulgurites, or lightning-written glass roots: a broken fork of fused sand grows into a branching glass-boned dragon. Its lightning shape is its actual body structure rather than a bolt marking on an animal.
evolution_design: A Y-shaped dark glass fork stands on two blunt sandy feet; one open branch socket contains a bright eye.
The fork grows into a powerful upright glass body, paired thick branching forearms, two angular glass legs and a three-pronged crown; hollow branch ends form the eyes and discharge points.

silhouettes.front: Thick Y-fork glass body and two sandy feet.
silhouettes.back: Back glass fork and socket rim.

silhouettes.front: Broad upright branching glass dragon with two sturdy legs and three crown prongs.
silhouettes.back: Forked glass nape and thick upper branch shoulders; legs cropped.

families.habitat: Storm-exposed Minnesota sand prairie. This is an ecological/geological inference, not a claimed verified Minnesota fulgurite collecting locality.

sources.evidence: Lightning can fuse sand into branched glass tubes called fulgurites; the cited example is in Colorado.
sources.fantasy_extension: The general process is combined with Minnesota storm and sand-prairie habitat to invent a living glass-root creature.

sources.evidence: The Agassiz landscape includes sandy deposits and old shoreline ridges.
sources.fantasy_extension: Provides Minnesota habitat context without inventing a documented mineral occurrence.

families.theme: Ants, honeydew bargaining and living toll gates: a sly collector grows a glossy honeydrop reservoir, small scoop mandibles and six soft curved legs that brace into a low barrier. It trades passage for sweet sap, building the gate out of its own six limbs rather than wearing a guard uniform. The honeydew reservoir also stores a fictional sour defensive secretion, delivered by the scoop jaws; no claim is made about the toxicity of real honeydew.
evolution_design: A round-headed six-legged nectar collector with small spoon mandibles, dew-beaded antennae and a glossy pear-shaped honeydew reservoir.

The honeydrop reservoir becomes the dominant rounded body mass. Six curved legs brace into a low living barrier while the front pair offer sweet sap in cupped scoop feet. The small jaws deliver stored sour secretion without growing into armor or tusks.

silhouettes.front: Round purple ant head, small scoop smile, dew-beaded antennae and a plump golden honeydrop abdomen.
silhouettes.back: Glossy honeydrop reservoir in the foreground, rounded back of head and soft antennae aimed away.

silhouettes.front: Huge glossy honeydrop reservoir, a small friendly head and six curved legs bracing a broad low gate stance.
